q_slogan: The Fourier transform of the function J₂ at a point w in 8-dimensional real space is equal to the curve integral of a certain complex one-form along the straight line from -1 + i to i in the complex plane, where the one-form is built from the function Ψ₁_fourier evaluated at the squared norm of w.
c_slogan: The Fourier transform of the function that maps w to psi(x times Q(w)) is given by a constant factor involving gamma and the determinant of xJ, multiplied by the complex conjugate of psi evaluated at x inverse times the dual quadratic form Q applied to w. The value of gamma depends on whether the field F is real or complex, and in the real case it is determined by the signature of the matrix xJ. The measure used is a product of Lebesgue measures adjusted by a factor depending on the field. This result follows from general theorems on second-degree characters in Weil's work.

q_slogan: For each natural number i, deriv_lbQ(i) gives a rational number that is guaranteed to be less than or equal to the value of 2 times Acoeff(i) plus Bcoeff(i) times u, evaluated at t = 1, where u is a rigorous rational approximation of 1/pi chosen based on the sign of Bcoeff(i).
c_slogan: The value of pi at 2i+1 is less than or equal to the ratio of n1 over n2 raised to the power of (2i-2) times alpha, multiplied by the value of pi at 3, where alpha is between 0 and 1.

q_slogan: The function TimeMan.val is a continuous, injective, and open map from the time manifold to the real numbers, meaning it embeds the time manifold as an open subset of the reals while preserving its topological structure. It is also surjective, so it maps the time manifold onto the entire real line. Together, this means TimeMan.val is a homeomorphism between the time manifold and the real numbers.
c_slogan: A time-change function is a continuous, increasing, and onto function that maps the interval from 0 to T1 onto the interval from 0 to T2.

q_slogan: The sum of the squared absolute values of the elements in the second row of a CKM matrix equals 1, where the squared absolute value of a complex number is computed as the norm squared. This means the second row of the matrix is normalized when using the standard complex norm.

c_slogan: For a language L and a set of natural numbers H, the H-power of L is the set of all strings formed by repeating each string in L exactly k times, for every k in H. When H is all natural numbers, this is simply called the power of L. The notation L^(k) means each string in L is repeated k times. The notation L^(H) or pow_H(L) represents the union of all such repeated strings for k in H.

q_slogan: The electromagnetic potential of a harmonic wave traveling in the x-direction has a value of zero for the time component at any point in spacetime, when evaluated using the left injection of 0 into the sum type representing indices. q_slogan: Raising a physical dimension to a natural number power multiplies its mass exponent by that number. c_slogan: Dimensions are represented as lists of numbers, where each number tracks the power of a base unit. The zero dimension is a list of zeros, multiplying dimensions adds their list elements pairwise, raising a dimension to a power multiplies each element by that power, and inverting a dimension negates each element. These operations allow efficient computation of physical dimensions in unit checking.

q_slogan: The declaration defines a bijection between the quotient space of centers under lattice translations and a set of center points that lie within a fundamental domain of the lattice, where the fundamental domain is determined by a chosen integer basis. The result relies on the fact that the fundamental domain contains exactly one representative from each coset of the lattice.
c_slogan: There is a region in space that represents the fundamental domain of a lattice, and when this region is shifted by all elements of the lattice, the resulting collection of regions only overlaps finitely many times in any bounded area.

q_slogan: The theorem states that if a list of boxes contains a point where a function reaches its minimum value within a given domain, and each box is valid, then after applying the core minimization step, the updated list of boxes will still contain a box with a value at least as low as the original minimum. This ensures the optimization process does not lose track of potential minimum values. It uses rational number arithmetic and interval evaluations to preserve correctness.
c_slogan: The optimization process iteratively reduces a finite set of possible function values by using counterexamples, until no smaller values can be found, at which point the current candidate is the minimum. Each iteration removes values larger than the current best candidate, ensuring progress toward the smallest value. Since the initial set is finite, the process eventually empties the set of smaller candidates, confirming the optimum. This method guarantees finding the global minimum for finite search domains.

q_slogan: For a natural number n with a prime factorization f, if the total imbalance of f is zero, then the logarithm of n multiplied by the number of prime factors (counted with multiplicity) equals the logarithm of n factorial plus the difference between the sum of the logs of the prime factors and the log of n. This difference is called the "waste" and measures how closely the factorization matches n. When the waste is zero, the product of the prime powers in the factorization exactly equals n.
c_slogan: The number of distinct prime factors of n factorial equals the number of primes up to n, and the total number of prime factors of n factorial counting multiplicity is given by a sum involving primes. The count of distinct prime factors of n factorial is approximately n divided by the logarithm of n, with a small error term. The total number of prime factors of n factorial is approximately n times the sum of the log log of n and two constants related to prime numbers, again with a small error term.
